subject: [Invite] NeurIPS AI leaders dinner, 2nd Dec
text:
Hi [NAME],

Noticed your NeurIPS paper submission - congrats, seriously impressive work.

I'm reaching out to invite you to a small dinner our co-founders, [SENDER] and [SENDER], are hosting on 2nd December at 6:30pm at Herb & Wood, a short walk from the venue.

We're celebrating the launch of our open-source multimodal dataset (E-MM1), and a handful of AI/ML leaders and researchers will be joining (including teams from Woven by Toyota, 1X, and Netradyne).

If you haven't come across us before, Encord is a multimodal data development platform used by frontier AI teams across robotics, AV, VLMs and multimodal AI applications.

Let me know if you'd like to join as we'd love to have you there, and I can send over the details.

-[SENDER]

P.S. If dinner's tricky, we're also hosting drinks on 3rd Dec and will be at booth #642 all week

subject: Data Platform for Perception Teams
text:
Hi [NAME],

We've been working with perception teams at Boston Dynamics, Toyota Woven
and 1X Robotics on multimodal ML workflows.

Encord's data engine lets teams work directly with 3D point clouds, LiDAR,
radar, and multi-sensor data alongside video in a single pipeline.

Teams are using it to build crisp, high-fidelity annotations and to unify
what would otherwise be siloed 2D, 3D, and sensor workflows.

Is this something that would be relevant for your work? If not, is there a
team at [COMPANY] who owns multimodal perception data that might benefit
from a unified platform?

subject: Invitation to speak - Physical AI panel
text:
Hi [NAME],

I enjoyed your recent piece on Humanoids and Dexterous learning -
particularly your emphasis on richer sensor data beyond vision. Your
perspective has been a major inspiration for an upcoming Physical AI panel
I'm organising - co-hosted by Encord, Weights & Biases, and Anyscale.

We'd be honoured to have you join as a *panelist*. The event will take
place on the *evening of January 27, [YEAR]* at the W&B's office in SF.

We see now as an important moment for Physical AI, with new models, data,
and hardware breakthroughs announced everyday, and believe your decades of
experience and contrarian viewpoint would help anchor the discussion. We
expect the panel to explore:

   - Real-world data collection & quality management
   - Sim-to-real gap & experiment tracking
   - Infrastructure management & inference optimization

I'd love to feature your perspectives on these themes. Would you have 20
mins next week to go over details?

subject: Data Layer for Labeling w/ Deep Mind
text:
Hey [NAME],

One pattern we're seeing with our customers like 1X Robotics and Boston
Dynamics is that even with frontier VLA models, you still need a strong
robot-specific data engine.

Encord helps humanoid teams turn teleop demos and multi-camera/depth
sequences into clean, versioned datasets for training and regression
testing.

It's how they mine edge cases, keep manipulation/locomotion evaluation
consistent, and tighten the perception→action loop as hardware evolves.

I'd invite you to check out [LINK] and let me know what you think.

subject: Annotate Platform for CV Teams
text:
Hey [NAME],

We recently started working with health based application for video
tracking and object detection at scale.

We offer a full data engine that allows for you to pre-label with best in
class models like [SENDER]-3 and use humans in the loop to validate. We also
have video, 2D, 3D and LiDAR natively supported.

These detections can improve your users workout experience by tracking
form, rep counts etc.

I'd invite you to check out [LINK] and let me know what you think!

subject: Bridging CV + LLM Workflows at Hinge
text:
Hi [NAME],

We met with Philippe and Sohail last year when your team was scaling the CV
pipeline, and with Movement Analysis now live, it feels like the right time
to reconnect.

A lot of teams we work with are struggling to bridge CV outputs with
LLM-driven guidance. Encord's multimodal workflow helps unify those
pipelines inside secure healthcare VPCs and catch the CV edge cases that
break downstream LLM reasoning

Would you or someone on your team be open for a brief discussion?

-[SENDER]
